svg.text: The geometry of a network — and its growth law — depend on the scale you look at.
Edges are chains of smaller nodes; the chains meet at connector vertices.
You are inside a chain. Walk, and you stay on a line.
You reach connector vertices; the chains close into polygons.
Further out the network keeps adding detail: crevices upon crevices.
The point: the network is one-dimensional to something small enough to be stuck inside a chain; two-dimensional to something big enough to see the
polygons; and hyperbolic to something bigger still, because it keeps adding detail as you move away from the centre — so its curvature is itself a
function of scale. Entities at different scales inhabit fundamentally different worlds, with different distance and growth functions relative to their environment.
